newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chip firms drive Moroccan bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip firms drive Moroccan bourse higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market ended its two-hour session on Thursday higher pulled up largely by blue chip companies, including conglomerate ONA Group, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 437.15 points, up 0.30 percent compared with Wednesday's session.
"The ONA's and Wafabank surge was the engine behind the bourse index rise for the second consecutive day," a Casablanca-based market analyst said.
ONA, Morocco's largest private conglomerate which has diversified stakes in 100 companies, jumped ten dirhams to close at 495 dirhams, he said.
ONA Group, showed a 20.6 percent rise in its consolidated net profit to 328.6 million dirhams in the period of January-June 1996 compared with 272.4 million dirhams in the first half of 1995.
Detailed results were announced by ONA's president Fouad Filali following a meeting of the conglomerate's board of directors.
ONA and its subsidiaries control between 65 and 80 percent of Morocco's edible oil, sugar and milk market, stockbrokers said.

The conglomerate's listed subsidiaries sugar refinery Cosumar, agro-industry Centrale Laitiere, edible oil firm Lesieur and Financiere Diwan, all together posted positive results in the first half of 1996 compared with the same period last year, the group said.
Wafabank, one of the country largest banks, rose 15 dirhams to close at 520 dirhams.
The traded volume on the official market was 14.5 million dirhams compared with 20.5 million on Wednesday. ($1= 8.7 dirhams)
